questions.question: 'The Last Lesson' is set in the days of
questions.answer:
**(A)** the Franco-Prussian War

The story is set in **1870–71**, in the closing days of the **Franco-Prussian War**, when Prussia had defeated France and the order came from Berlin that only German would be taught in the schools of **Alsace and Lorraine**. That order is the "last lesson" of M. Hamel.

questions.question: When and where was the Annual Convention of the Indian National Congress party held?
questions.answer:
**(C)** December 1916, Lucknow

The **annual convention of the Indian National Congress was held at Lucknow in December 1916** — the famous Lucknow session at which the Congress and the Muslim League agreed on a common programme. It was there that **Rajkumar Shukla** came to Gandhiji with the grievances of the Champaran peasants.

questions.question: What is the story 'Deep Water' speaking about?
options: Fear of water and the way to overcome it
Fear of people and the way to overcome it
Fear of dogs and the way to overcome it
Fear of swimming and the way to overcome it
questions.answer:
**(A)** Fear of water and the way to overcome it

"Deep Water" is about **fear — and about how an irrational fear can be mastered**. Douglas nearly drowns twice, is left with a terror of water that spoils his life, and then hires an instructor, practises for months and deliberately faces the deep water until "**all we have to fear is fear itself**".

questions.question: Where was Saheb employed?
questions.answer:
**(A)** at a tea stall

At the end of "Lost Spring" Saheb works **at a tea stall** for **eight hundred rupees and all his meals** — a job that gives him money but takes away his freedom. The steel canister he carries is "**not his**", and the author says his face has lost the "**carefree look**" of the ragpicker.

questions.question: Whom did Gandhiji send a telegram to, in Muzaffarpur?
questions.answer:
**(C)** J. B. Kripalani

On the way to Champaran, Gandhi stopped at **Muzaffarpur** and sent a telegram to **Professor J. B. Kripalani**, asking him to come with a car to take him to the home of Professor Malkani. Kripalani met him at the station at midnight. (*The solved booklet ticks Rajkumar Shukla; Shukla was with him, and the telegram went to Kripalani.*)

questions.question: Which of the following can be added to make article writing interesting?
questions.answer:
**(C)** Both (A) and (B)

A good article is made interesting by **quotations** (they give it a voice and an authority) **and by statistics** (they give it weight and proof). Both are used sparingly, to support the writer's own argument, never to replace it.

questions.question: While writing notices the signature of the issuing authority should be written at the
questions.answer:
**(A)** bottom

The **signature of the issuing authority is written at the bottom, on the left**, with the name of the office held below it (Head Boy, Secretary, Principal). The top is reserved for the name of the institution.

questions.question: What is the motive of writing a letter to the editor?
options: To ask him to take action
To threaten him to take action
To order him to take action
To request him to give some space in his newspaper's letter to editor column
questions.answer:
**(D)** to request space in the editor's column

A letter to the editor is written **to reach the public through the newspaper** — to place a grievance or an opinion before a wide readership in the hope that the authorities will notice it. The editor is not asked to act, still less ordered or threatened; he is requested to publish.

questions.question: What is written on the top while writing a notice?
questions.answer:
**(A)** Name of organization

The **name of the organisation or institution is written at the very top, in capitals**, followed by the word NOTICE, the date, the heading and the body. The notice speaks in the institution's name, and so the institution is named first.

questions.question: A formal letter starts with
questions.answer:
**(C)** Sender's address

A formal letter begins with the **sender's address** (with the date below it, or at the top right in the traditional format), then the receiver's address, the subject, the salutation and the body. The writer must be identified before the person written to.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct for report writing?
options: A report may use slang words
A report must be creative, not factual
A report presents facts and observations logically
questions.answer:
**(C)** A report presents facts and observations logically

A report is **factual, objective and orderly**: it gives what happened, when, where and to whom, in a sequence a reader can follow. It is not the place for **slang**, for invention in place of facts, or for **humour** at the expense of accuracy.

questions.question: Speech writing is a formal and verbal communication to
questions.answer:
**(D)** All of these

A speech is a **formal, spoken communication** meant to deliver **thoughts**, to convey a **message**, and to put **opinions and perspectives** before an audience. The one correction to the third option is that a speech is heard, not read; the purpose it names is the same.

questions.question: Pablo Neruda wants the entire humanity to
questions.answer:
**(D)** keep still

The poem opens, "Now we will count to twelve / and we will all **keep still**." Neruda asks all humanity for a moment of stillness and silence — "not total inactivity", he insists, but a pause in which we may see ourselves and each other.

questions.question: Identify the literary device in 'like late winter's moon'.
questions.answer:
**(A)** Simile

The mother's face is compared to "**a late winter's moon**" with the word **"like"** — "her face ashen like that of a corpse... **like that of a corpse**", and again "**pale as a late winter's moon**". The explicit comparison makes it a **simile**, not a metaphor.

questions.question: Who is Endymion in the poem 'A Thing of Beauty'?
questions.answer:
**(D)** a young shepherd

**Endymion** is the beautiful **young shepherd** of Greek myth whom the moon goddess Selene loved and lulled into an eternal sleep. Keats names him in the poem beside the "**musk-rose blooms**" and the "**grandeur of the dooms**" — his story is one of the "**lovely tales**" that make beauty a joy for ever.

questions.question: Who wanted a photograph of himself holding the gun and standing over the tiger's carcass?
questions.answer:
**(D)** the king

It is the **Maharaja** — the Tiger King — who, after every kill, wanted the ceremony of the photograph: himself with his gun, standing over the tiger's carcass. The trophy photographs are part of the vanity the story mocks, and the hundredth "tiger" that finally kills him was a wooden toy.

questions.chapter: Journey to the End of the Earth
questions.question: The name of the programme that takes high school students to the end of the earth is
questions.answer:
**(D)** Students on Ice

The programme is "**Students on Ice**", founded by the Canadian **Geoff Green**. It takes school and college students to the polar regions so that they may see the ice and the wildlife for themselves and understand how fragile the earth's systems are.

questions.chapter: Journey to the End of the Earth
questions.question: Gondwana existed roughly around
questions.answer:
**(C)** 250 million years ago

The southern supercontinent **Gondwana** — which carried India, South America, Africa, Antarctica and Australia — existed roughly **250 million years ago**, before the continents drifted apart. It is because of that single land mass that the rocks and fossils of Antarctica match those of India.

questions.question: Sadao went to America to learn
questions.answer:
**(B)** surgery and medicine

Dr. Sadao Hoki "had been sent to America to learn **surgery and medicine**", and he returned "the best surgeon in Japan". It is that training which makes him able to cut the bullet out of the wounded American — and his skill which makes the dilemma his.

questions.question: What percentage did the British planters agree to repay the Indigo planters?
questions.answer:
**(C)** 25 per cent

When the peasants demanded their money back, the British landlords offered to **refund 25 per cent** — "they thought the peasants would accept it". Gandhi asked for 50 per cent; the landlords offered 25, and Gandhi accepted, because the **amount mattered less than the fact of surrender**: "the landlords had to surrender part of the money and, with it, part of their prestige".

questions.question: Why was Louisa, Charley's wife, worried?
questions.answer:
**(A)** knowing the incident

Louisa was worried because she **knew about the third level** — Charley's tale of getting off a train at a station of 1894 — and she feared his "**waking-dream wish to escape**" was taking him over. She took him to his psychiatrist friend Sam to have it explained away.

questions.question: What does the metaphor Rattrap in the lesson signify?
questions.answer:
**(D)** human greed and distraction

The peddler's theory is that the world is a **rattrap**: it offers baits — riches, food, shelter, comfort — and "once the bait is taken, the trap closes". The metaphor stands for **human greed and the distractions** that snare a man; in the story the thirty kronor are the bait.

questions.question: Who is the poet of the poem 'Aunt Jennifer's Tigers'?
questions.answer:
**(A)** Adrienne Rich

"Aunt Jennifer's Tigers" is by the American poet **Adrienne Rich** (1929–2012). It is one of her earliest poems, and its subject — a woman whose art is freer than her life — runs through all her later work.

questions.question: The founder of Gemini Studios was
questions.answer:
**(B)** S. S. Vasan

The Gemini Studios of "Poets and Pancakes" was founded by **S. S. Vasan**, the "**boss**" of the chapter — the man whose "**encyclopaedic**" knowledge Asokamitran records, and beside whom Subbu was the most gifted of his staff.

questions.question: What was Maharaja's preference for marrying a girl?
options: She must have tigers in her state
questions.answer:
**(D)** she must have tigers in her state

The Maharaja's "**master strategy**" was to marry into a state with a **large tiger population**, so that he could kill five or six tigers on every visit to his father-in-law. He had already killed seventy in his own kingdom and needed more if he was to reach a hundred.

questions.question: What does V. S. Naipaul feel about interviews?
questions.answer:
**(D)** None of these

None of the three words describes Naipaul's view. What the chapter says is that Naipaul "**feels that some people are wounded by interviews and lose a part of themselves**" — a sense of **injury and loss**, not horror (which is Lewis Carroll's "just horror of the interviewer"), nor happiness, nor desire.

questions.question: To whom did Sophie tell her secret out first?
questions.answer:
**(B)** her brother Geoff

Sophie tells **Geoff** first. Sitting in his room while he works on his motorbike, she announces that she met **Danny Casey**, and it is Geoff's quiet attention — "he was impressed" — that makes the invention worth keeping alive. (*The solved booklet ticks Jansie; the story's order is Geoff first, and the secret grows in his silence.*)

questions.question: Who is Mr. Lamb?
options: An old man with an artificial leg
questions.answer:
**(A)** an old man with an artificial leg

Mr. Lamb is an **old man who has lost one leg** — he has a tin leg, and he lives alone in a house with a garden and an apple orchard. He is not Derry's grandfather but the stranger whose **own disfigurement** makes him the only person able to talk to the boy.

questions.question: Annan is the elder brother of
questions.answer:
**(C)** Bama

**Annan** is **Bama's elder brother**. He is the one who explains to her why the old man carried the packet of food by its string, and who tells her that "**we too are human beings**" and that **education** is the way to escape the humiliation of caste.

questions.question: Why did Zitkala hide herself?
options: To save herself from a woman
To save herself from other children
To stop people from cutting her hair
questions.answer:
**(D)** to stop people from cutting her hair

When Judewin warns her that the palefaces will cut her hair, Zitkala-Sa **hides under a bed** in a dark corner of the room — because among her people a shingled head was worn only by cowards and mourners. She is dragged out, tied to a chair and her hair is cut: "**I lost my spirit**", she writes.

**The protest.** Her hiding is the child's first act of **defiance**, and the memory of it shaped her later work for her people.

questions.question:
Read the passage on Marie Curie and answer any six of the following:
(a) Who was Marie Curie, and what were her major scientific achievements?
(b) What elements did Marie and Pierre Curie study and discover?
(c) Where and when was Marie Curie born?
(d) Why was Marie unable to study at the University of Warsaw?
(e) Which university did Marie Curie attend in France, and what degrees did she earn there?
(f) Who did Marie meet at the Sorbonne, and what was his contribution to her life?
(g) What tragic event happened to Pierre Curie, and when did it occur?
(h) Write the correct meaning of the words from the passage: (i) invention (ii) misfortune.
questions.answer:
### (a)

**Answer.** Marie Curie was "**one of the most accomplished scientists in history**". With her husband **Pierre**, she **discovered radium** — "an element widely used for treating cancer" — and **studied uranium and other radioactive substances**.

**The passage's own words.**

> "Together with her husband, Pierre, she discovered radium, an element widely used for treating cancer, and studied uranium and other radioactive substances."

**Her achievements in the passage.** (i) The discovery of **radium**; (ii) her study of **uranium and radioactivity**, which helped "**unlock the secrets of the atom**"; (iii) the **first woman professor** at the Sorbonne, where she succeeded her husband; and (iv) the **Nobel Prize in chemistry in 1911** "for isolating radium".

### (b)

**Answer.** They **discovered radium** and **studied uranium** and other radioactive substances.

**The passage's own words.**

> "...she discovered radium, an element widely used for treating cancer, and studied uranium and other radioactive substances."

**The two words to keep apart.** **Uranium** was the substance they *studied* (it was already known, and its rays were the clue that led them on); **radium** was the element they *discovered*. Their work on both "later helped to unlock the secrets of the atom".

### (c)

**Answer.** She was born in **Warsaw, Poland, in 1867**.

**The passage's own words.**

> "Marie was born in 1867 in Warsaw, Poland, where her father was a professor of physics."

**Why the details matter.** Her **Polish** birth explains the obstacle she faced: the **University of Warsaw was closed to women**, so she had to leave her country for Paris to study. Her father's being "a professor of physics" explains her "**great exuberance for learning**".

### (d)

**Answer.** Because "**the university in Warsaw was closed to women**".

**The passage's own words.**

> "She became disgruntled, when she learned that the university in Warsaw was closed to women."

**What she did instead.** "However determined to receive a higher education, she **defiantly left Poland** and in **1891 entered the Sorbonne**, a French university." The word "defiantly" is the passage's judgement on the exclusion — and on her answer to it.

### (e)

**Answer.** She attended the **Sorbonne**, a French university, entering it in **1891**, and there she "**earned her master's degree and doctorate in physics**".

**The passage's own words.**

> "...she defiantly left Poland and in 1891 entered the Sorbonne, a French university, where she earned her master's degree and doctorate in physics."

**Later at the same university.** She was later "asked to succeed her husband as a **physics professor at the Sorbonne**", becoming "the **first woman** to be given a professorship at the world-famous university".

### (f)

**Answer.** At the Sorbonne she met **Pierre Curie**, one of "the greatest scientists of her day". He became her **husband** (they married in **1895**) and her **research partner**.

**The passage's own words.**

> "Marie was fortunate to have studied at the Sorbonne with some of the greatest scientists of her day, one of whom was Pierre Curie. Marie and Pierre were married in 1895 and spent many productive years working together in the physics laboratory."

**His contribution.** Together they **discovered radium** and studied radioactivity; "**Pierre and Marie's amicable collaboration** later helped to unlock the secrets of the atom". His death in 1906 was the great grief of her life.

### (g)

**Answer.** "**A short time after they discovered radium**", Pierre was **killed by a horse-drawn wagon, in 1906**.

**The passage's own words.**

> "A short time after they discovered radium, Pierre was killed by a horse-drawn wagon in 1906."

**Its effect on Marie.** She "was **stunned** by this horrible misfortune and endured **heartbreaking anguish**", and her distress was "greatly increased" by the fact that she had "**two young daughters to raise by herself**". Out of that grief she took up his chair at the Sorbonne.

### (h)

**Answer.** (i) Invention — **discovery**; (ii) Misfortune — **mishap / bad luck** (the passage's own word for it is "misfortune", and the event itself is "**this horrible misfortune**").

**As used in the passage.**

> "...she discovered radium..." — a **discovery**, not an invention, because radium existed already and was found, not made.

> "Marie was stunned by this **horrible misfortune**..." — the accident that killed Pierre, i.e. a piece of **bad luck, a calamity**.

**Note.** The distinction in (i) is worth remembering: one **invents** a machine and **discovers** an element. The passage uses "discovered" of radium throughout.

questions.question:
Read the following passage carefully and make notes on it using headings and sub-headings. Use recognisable abbreviations, wherever necessary. Give a suitable title.

Healthy eating means having the right kind of food in the right amount. Our body needs different nutrients to grow, stay strong, and work properly. These include carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals, and water. Each of these plays an important role. Carbohydrates give us energy, proteins help build and repair body tissues, fats keep us warm and protect our organs, while vitamins and minerals keep our body systems healthy.

A balanced diet includes food from all these groups in the correct amounts. Fruits, vegetables, grains, milk, eggs, and pulses are all important for a healthy diet. Eating too much junk food like chips, sweets, and soft drinks can lead to obesity and other health problems. It is also important to drink plenty of water and eat fresh food instead of packaged or processed food.

Good eating habits should start early in life. Children should be taught to eat slowly, chew properly, and avoid skipping meals. Breakfast is the most important meal of the day because it gives energy after a night's rest. Along with healthy eating, regular exercise is equally important. Physical activities like walking, running, or playing games help the body stay fit and strong.

Healthy eating is not about strict rules or giving up all your favourite foods. It is about balance and moderation. By making small, smart choices everyday, anyone can develop a healthy lifestyle that keeps the body fit, the mind active, and life happier.
questions.answer:
**Answer.**

**Title: Healthy Eating for a Healthy Life**

**1. What healthy eating means**
   1.1 right kind of food in right amount
   1.2 body needs nutrients: carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals, water

**2. Role of each nutrient**
   2.1 carbohydrates → energy
   2.2 proteins → build & repair body tissues
   2.3 fats → keep warm, protect organs
   2.4 vitamins & minerals → keep body systems healthy

**3. A balanced diet**
   3.1 food from all groups in correct amounts
   3.2 fruits, vegetables, grains, milk, eggs, pulses
   3.3 too much junk food (chips, sweets, soft drinks) → obesity & other health problems
   3.4 plenty of water; fresh food rather than packaged/processed food

**4. Good eating habits**
   4.1 start early in life
   4.2 eat slowly, chew properly, do not skip meals
   4.3 breakfast — most imp. meal; gives energy after night's rest

**5. Exercise & balance**
   5.1 regular exercise equally imp. — walking, running, games
   5.2 not strict rules or giving up favourite foods
   5.3 balance & moderation; small smart choices → fit body, active mind, happier life

**Abbreviations used:** imp. = important; & = and; → = leads to; e.g. = for example; nutri. = nutrition; reg. = regular.

**Note on the form.** Notes are in **phrases, not sentences**, arranged in a **numbered outline** with indentation for sub-points, using **recognisable abbreviations and symbols**, and always under a **title**.

questions.question: Write a summary of the passage given in Q. 39 in about 80 words.
questions.answer:
**Answer.** Healthy eating means the right food in the right amount. The body needs carbohydrates for energy, proteins to build and repair tissues, fats for warmth and protection, vitamins and minerals for healthy systems, and plenty of water. A balanced diet draws on fruits, vegetables, grains, milk, eggs and pulses, and avoids junk food, which causes obesity. Habits should start early: eat slowly, chew well, never skip breakfast, and exercise daily. Healthy eating is not strict denial but balance and moderation.

**The summary in one line.** A balanced diet of the right nutrients, sensible habits from childhood and daily exercise together keep the body fit and the mind active.

**Note on the form.** A summary keeps **only the main ideas, in your own words, in one paragraph**, in about the number of words asked, with no quotation, no examples beyond what is essential, and no personal opinion.

questions.question: What things did Franz find more tempting than going to school? (Answer in not more than 50 words.)
questions.answer:
**Answer.** Franz found the **warm, bright morning** more tempting than school: the day was "**warm and bright**", the birds were chirping at the edge of the woods, and the **Prussians drilling** in the open field behind the sawmill drew him.

Above all he wanted to **look for birds' eggs** and to **go sliding on the saar** — and he was afraid of M. Hamel's questions on participles.

questions.question: What did the city people complain about in the poem 'A Roadside Stand'? (Answer in not more than 50 words.)
questions.answer:
**Answer.** The city people complained that the **roadside stand spoiled the view** — it was "**a wild and wretched**" thing, an eyesore on the landscape of the "polished traffic". They also complained that the stand was useless and that "**the flowers and the fruit**" were badly arranged.

**The poet's irony.** They complain about the look of the stand, never about the poverty that built it.

questions.question: What did the peddler sell and how did he make the things? (Answer in not more than 50 words.)
questions.answer:
**Answer.** The peddler sold **rattraps** — small wire traps for rats — which he made himself out of "**wire**" begged or stolen from the farms. The work brought in almost nothing, so he had to **beg** and occasionally **steal** to keep body and soul together.

**The metaphor he made.** He also sold an idea: that the world is a rattrap.

questions.question: Why did Rajkumar Shukla want to take Gandhiji to Champaran? (Answer in not more than 50 words.)
questions.answer:
**Answer.** Shukla wanted Gandhi to see for himself the **injustice of the British landlord system** in Champaran, where the peasants were **forced to grow indigo** on part of their land and surrender the harvest as rent, and later made to **pay to be released** from the arrangement.

He was "**illiterate but resolute**" and would not let Gandhi refuse.

questions.question: Why did Dr. Sadao seek Hana's help to treat the American soldier? (Answer in not more than 50 words.)
questions.answer:
**Answer.** Because the operation had to be done at home, where there was no nurse, and Hana was the only person he could trust.

He needed her to **hold the patient** and give the anaesthetic while he cut out the bullet, and he needed her **company and courage**, since the servants had refused to enter the room.

questions.question: What did M. Hamel say about the French language? Why did he think that language is the key to prison when people are enslaved? (Answer in about 80–100 words.)
questions.answer:
**Answer.** M. Hamel calls French "**the most beautiful language in the world — the clearest, the most logical**", and tells his class to "**guard it and never forget it**", because "when a people are enslaved, as long as they hold fast to their language it is as if they held **the key to their prison**".

**What the image means.** A conquered people can be made to lose its land, its laws and its schools, but if it keeps its language it keeps its memory, its literature and its sense of itself — and with them the means of one day becoming free. The language is the key, because the prison door can be opened from inside.

**The irony.** The order from Berlin has just taken the key away from Alsace, and M. Hamel's last lesson is an attempt to press it into the children's hands before he goes.

questions.chapter: Journey to the End of the Earth
questions.question: 'The world's geological history is trapped in Antarctica.' How is the study of this region useful to us? (Answer in about 80–100 words.)
questions.answer:
**Answer.** Antarctica holds the record of the planet in its **ice and rock**, and studying it tells us how the earth was made and where it is going.

**How the study helps.**
1. **The past.** Six hundred and fifty million years ago Antarctica was a warm part of **Gondwana**; its fossils of **giant ammonites and dinosaurs** and its rocks match those of India and South America, and prove the theory of **continental drift**.
2. **The present.** Its ice core records the **carbon dioxide** of a million years and so explains "**climate change**"; its ice holds **70 per cent of the world's fresh water**.
3. **The future.** Its krill and plankton are the base of the ocean's food chain, and its minerals and oil are a temptation we must learn to resist.

**The lesson.** It teaches us, in Tishani Doshi's words, that we are "**the most dangerous animals**" on a fragile planet, and that "**what we do now will affect the future**".

questions.question: You are Aditya Singh/Aditi Singh, a student of Class 12, Sunrise Public School. Write a notice informing students about a Science Exhibition being held in your school. (Answer within 50 words.)
questions.answer:
**Answer.**

**SUNRISE PUBLIC SCHOOL**

**NOTICE**

*10 September 2026*

**SCIENCE EXHIBITION**

A Science Exhibition will be held in the school hall on **25 September 2026** from 10 a.m. to 3 p.m. Students of Classes IX to XII may register their models with their science teachers by **18 September**. Parents are invited.

**Aditi Singh**
Class XII-A

**Keep it short.** In about 50 words: **what, when, where, whom to register with and by when**, plus the signature — and no unnecessary detail.

questions.question: You are Santosh Rajwar/Santoshi Rajwar, Secretary of the Environment Club. Write a notice about a Tree Plantation Drive to be conducted in your school campus. (Answer within 50 words.)
questions.answer:
**Answer.**

**SUNRISE PUBLIC SCHOOL — ENVIRONMENT CLUB**

**NOTICE**

*14 July 2026*

**TREE PLANTATION DRIVE**

The Environment Club will hold a **tree plantation drive** in the school campus on **Saturday, 20 July 2026, at 8 a.m.** Students who wish to take part should give their names to their class teachers by **18 July**.

**Santoshi Rajwar**
Secretary, Environment Club

**Keep it short.** In about 50 words: the **event, date, time, venue, whom to give names to and the last date** — with the signature and the office held.

questions.question: You are Anita Singh, a resident of 45, Lajpat Nagar, New Delhi. Write a letter to the Editor of 'The Hindustan Times' expressing concern about the rising cases of theft and chain-snatching in your locality and suggesting measures to control them. (Answer in about 100 words.)
questions.answer:
**Answer.**

**Anita Singh**
**45, Lajpat Nagar**
**New Delhi**
**9 August 2026**

The Editor
*The Hindustan Times*
New Delhi

**Subject: Rising theft and chain-snatching in Lajpat Nagar**

Sir

Through your esteemed daily I wish to draw the attention of the police and the authorities to the **rising cases of theft and chain-snatching in Lajpat Nagar**.

In the last month there have been six cases in our lane alone. Two-wheeler riders snatch chains from women returning from the market in the evening, and three houses were broken into at night while the families were away. Elderly residents are afraid to go out after dark, and the market has lost customers.

**The measures I suggest.** The police should increase **night patrolling** in the colony, install **CCTV cameras** at the main crossings, and keep a **beat constable** who can be reached on a known number. The RWAs could employ **watchmen** and repair the street lights, since darkness helps the snatchers. Installment **publicity on prevention** in Hindi would also help the older residents.

I hope publication of this letter will move the authorities to act before someone is hurt.

Yours faithfully
**Anita Singh**

**Format points.** Address and date, addressee, subject, the **complaint with particulars**, a set of **practical suggestions**, and a firm close — within 100 words.

questions.question: You are Amit Verma, a student of Class 12, Sunrise Public School. Your school celebrated 'Environment Day' last week. Write a report on the event highlighting the main activities and outcome. (Answer in about 100 words.)
questions.answer:
**Answer.**

**ENVIRONMENT DAY AT SUNRISE PUBLIC SCHOOL**

*By Amit Verma, Class XII*

**New Delhi, 7 June 2026.** Environment Day was celebrated at Sunrise Public School on 5 June with a **plantation drive, a poster competition and a pledge**, the programme running from 8 a.m. to noon.

**The activities.** The Principal planted a **neem sapling** in the school lawn, after which students of Classes IX to XII planted **a hundred saplings** along the boundary wall. An inter-house **poster competition** on "Save the Earth" was held in the art room, and the best three posters were displayed in the corridor. The science teacher then spoke on waste segregation and showed the school's new **two-bin system**.

**The outcome.** The day ended with an **environment pledge** administered to the whole assembly, and each class was given the charge of watering the saplings for a week in rotation. The Principal announced that a **paper-recycling drive** would follow next month.

**Format points.** Headline, byline, place and date, the **order of activities, the numbers and the result**, all in the past tense, without personal opinion.

questions.question: You are Sneha Nair, a student of Class 12. Write an article on 'The Importance of Reading Habits Among Students'. (Answer in about 100 words.)
questions.answer:
**Answer.**

**WHY A STUDENT MUST READ**

A student today carries a library in his pocket and reads less than ever. The habit of reading — of sitting with a book for an hour — is quietly disappearing, and with it something no screen can replace.

**Why reading matters.** A book demands patience and attention, the very qualities a stream of short videos destroys. Reading builds **vocabulary** and **expression**, which every examination and every interview rewards. It gives a student **knowledge beyond the syllabus** and, more important, the **ability to imagine another person's life** — the root of sympathy and of judgement.

**How to begin.** With twenty minutes a day and a book that is genuinely enjoyed: a story, a biography, a travel book, even a good newspaper. Keep a phone away while reading. Discuss what is read with a friend or a teacher.

**The reward.** A reader is never bored and never entirely alone; and the habit, once formed, is a pleasure for life.

**Format points.** A title, the **problem, the value of reading, practical advice and a conclusion** — within 100 words.
